findings.title: Handle an unset embed_category before indexing the query result
findings.body: The category query can return no rows when embed_category was never configured, is blank, or names a deleted category. Indexing row zero then fails before the intended uncategorized fallback runs. This also happens on a fresh database and on sites that never enabled embedding, so the migration blocks installation or upgrade. Handle empty results explicitly, including the fallback query.

findings.title: Normalize legacy allowed-host entries during migration
findings.body: The old embedding configuration accepts entries such as http://example.com and https://example.com/some-path. This migration inserts those values verbatim, bypassing the new model's protocol/path normalization. EmbeddableHost.record_for_host compares the stored value against URI.host, which is only example.com, so migrated URL-form entries stop allowing comments and topic retrieval after upgrade. Normalize the legacy entries before inserting them.

findings.title: Quote legacy host values in the INSERT
findings.body: Each legacy allowed-host value is interpolated directly into a quoted SQL literal without escaping. URL-form entries can contain apostrophes in their paths, such as https://example.com/o'reilly; such a value produces invalid SQL and aborts the migration. Use bound parameters or the connection's quoting API rather than concatenating the setting value into SQL.

findings.title: Allow valid DNS names in host validation
findings.body: The new hostname regex limits the top-level domain to five letters and prohibits consecutive hyphens. Consequently, valid hosts such as blog.technology, example.museum, and the punycode hostname xn--bcher-kva.de cannot be added or edited through the embedding configuration. Use hostname validation that supports valid DNS labels and current top-level domains.

findings.title: Make port-qualified host entries match incoming URLs
findings.body: Validation accepts example.com:8080, and the normalization callback retains the port, but record_for_host compares that stored string with URI.host, which returns example.com without the port. A successfully saved port-qualified entry therefore never allows even http://example.com:8080 and never supplies its category during import. Normalize storage and lookup consistently, or compare the host and port explicitly.

findings.title: Enforce a unique normalized host-to-category mapping
findings.body: Neither the model nor the migration prevents multiple records for the same hostname, including differently cased variants. Administrators can therefore save the same host with different categories, while record_for_host silently selects the first matching record. The other relationship appears successfully configured but is ignored when importing topics. Enforce uniqueness on the normalized, case-insensitive hostname, including a database constraint.

findings.title: Guard missing host values before normalization
findings.body: The before_validation callback calls sub! on host unconditionally. Creating or updating a host with an embeddable_host payload that omits host assigns nil and raises NoMethodError before the format validator or render_json_error can run. Missing required input should produce a validation response rather than a server error; guard blank values before normalizing them.
